The next PR should be:

**`fix(checkout): isolate seat holds per checkout`**, referencing [roadmap issue #74](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/issues/74).

### Roadmap status

PR [#91](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/pull/91) moved the roadmap from `REAL_WORLD_ROADMAP.md` into GitHub issues and phase milestones. The repository now explicitly treats those issues as the source of truth ([AGENTS.md](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/AGENTS.md:703)).

| Roadmap area | Current state |
|---|---|
| Phase 0, #63–#67 | Complete |
| Phase 1, #68–#72 | Complete |
| P2.1, #73 | Complete |
| P2.2, #74 | Partially complete |
| P2.3, #75 | Waiting behind #74 |
| P2.4, #76 | Five main slices merged; rebooking split to #234 |
| P2.5, #77 | Not started |
| Phases 3–5 | Later work |

There are currently **no open PRs**, and local `main` is clean and synchronized at [`55f25db`](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/commit/55f25db413683aa2faa8e0ea53b0639a4117f712).

### Why this PR is next

PR [#257](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/pull/257) delivered the first #74 slice: expiring holds and automatic abandonment/release behavior. Its follow-up comment records a verified defect: `holderKey` is currently the user ID, so two checkout tabs belonging to the same user can release or refresh each other’s seats.

The current code confirms that:

- Hold claims and releases use `session.user.id` ([actions.ts](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/app/actions.ts:423)).
- `SeatClaim` anticipates a future checkout-scoped identity but does not have one yet ([seatHolds.ts](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/lib/seatHolds.ts:23)).
- The wizard does not create its request identifier until booking submission, after seats were held ([BookingCheckoutWizard.tsx](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/components/ui/BookingCheckoutWizard.tsx:696)).

The PR should:

- Establish a validated checkout identifier before the first hold.
- Scope claim, refresh, visibility, and release operations to that checkout.
- Ensure two tabs for one account cannot interfere with each other.
- Add database concurrency, component, and browser coverage.
- Leave atomic hold-to-booking conversion and the visible expiry/recovery countdown for subsequent #74 slices.

That is the smallest independently shippable slice and removes a prerequisite blocker before the more delicate transaction work.
